author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists each specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only specialty view of the existing directory at a dedicated page: every specialty the clinic knows, by stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name (first name before last), plus a grouping for veterinarians holding no specialty. One page, no pagination. Reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty by its stored name, and under each specialty the veterinarians who hold it, shown by full name with first name before last name (for example Helen Leary)
A veterinarian who holds no specialty appears under a 'no specialty' grouping rather than being omitted
Every specialty and the 'no specialty' grouping render on one page, with no pagination
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed by its stored name, with no veterinarians shown beneath it
Specialties, the veterinarians within each specialty, and the position of the 'no specialty' grouping are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
Any navigation entry or inbound link to the page (deferred to a possible follow-up)
notes: Inverse of REQ-VET-001. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md with narrowest-reading resolutions: sort order of specialties and veterinarians (taken as stable order, edge case 2); whether an unheld specialty still appears (taken as yes, edge case 1); position of the 'no specialty' grouping (taken as stable). No further product answer will come during the work.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001, same vet feature package and same server-rendered Thymeleaf pattern (system-design Overview; ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf). One small extension: a new lookup repository SpecialtyRepository mirroring PetTypeRepository, because 'every specialty the clinic knows' includes specialties held by no vet, which VetRepository.findAll() (vet-rooted, EAGER specialties) cannot reach. The specialty-keyed grouping and the no-specialty bucket are built in the controller as view shaping, consistent with the observed pattern of shaping/business logic living in controllers rather than a service layer. No new module, no new pattern, no ADR warranted.
integration_points: New GET /specialties.html method on VetController returning view vets/specialtyList; no pagination (unlike /vets.html)
VetController gains a second constructor dependency on SpecialtyRepository alongside VetRepository

SpecialtyRepository.findAll() (name-ordered, @Query ORDER BY s.name) supplies the full specialty set including unheld ones; vetRepository.findAll() (reused, cached) supplies vets with their EAGER specialties for the inversion

Model carries a name-ordered LinkedHashMap<String,List<Vet>> of specialty-name -> holders (empty list for an unheld specialty) plus a separate noSpecialtyVets List<Vet>; no new DTO type, consistent with passing entities to templates
specialtyList.html reuses fragments/layout with the 'vets' active tab; no nav entry added (deferred, NG unchanged)

patterns.description: Name-ordered lookup repository: extends JpaRepository, single @Query('... ORDER BY x.name') method. SpecialtyRepository copies this shape exactly.
Vet.getSpecialties() already sorts by NamedEntity.getName(); full name is firstName + ' ' + lastName as rendered in vetList.html:18; nrOfSpecialties==0 identifies the no-specialty bucket.
Table/layout and the existing #{vets},#{specialties},#{none} message keys to reuse for the new page's static text.

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 build-time gate walks templates and compares keys across all 11 message bundles; any new user-facing key used in specialtyList.html that is absent from even one bundle fails the build.
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing keys where possible (#{specialties} heading, #{none} for the empty holder case); for the 'no specialty' group label add one new key to ALL 11 messages*.properties files. No hard-coded page text.

risks.risk: Stable-order acceptance criterion: an arbitrary iteration order would be non-deterministic.
risks.mitigation: Specialties ordered by name via SpecialtyRepository query; vets within each group and in the no-specialty bucket sorted deterministically (lastName then firstName); the no-specialty group rendered in a fixed position (after all named specialties) — a stable, deterministic layout.

risks.risk: Keying the grouping by Specialty entity could collapse or mis-group on entity equality; two rows sharing a name is not modeled but conceivable.
risks.mitigation: Drive the ordered map off the name-ordered specialty list and key holder lists by specialty name (the stored name the page displays); acceptable given specialties are unique lookup values.

notes: Verdict minor, no ADR. Deviation from prd-entry file_targets: the specialty-fetch belongs on a new SpecialtyRepository (Specialty-rooted, mirrors PetTypeRepository, keeps the 'vets' cache semantically clean) rather than on VetRepository as the prd-entry listed; VetRepository is therefore left untouched. system-design.md Contracts updated: added SpecialtyRepository row, extended VetController and Specialty Implements to REQ-VET-003. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records present, skipped. Security/reliability: read-only GET, no new trust boundary, Thymeleaf auto-escaping covers XSS of vet/specialty names; consistent with the app's existing no-auth demonstration posture. Next step: route to feature-implementer for TDD implementation of the five prd-entry test_names.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods lack the `the{Subject}` prefix required by the project BDD naming school (docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming, effective 2026-07-31). `shouldListEverySpecialtyWithTheVeterinariansHoldingIt`, `shouldShowVeterinariansByFullName`, `shouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty`, `shouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePageWithoutPagination`, `shouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian` all follow the `should{Outcome}` pattern rather than the required `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` school. A subject is missing from every name; the reader cannot tell what component is under test without reading the body.
findings.fix: Rename all five to lead with `the{Subject}`: e.g. `theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithTheVeterinariansHoldingIt`, `theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName`, `theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty`, `theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllOnOnePageWithoutPagination`, `theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian`.

findings.description: `shouldShowVeterinariansByFullName` asserts only `content().string(containsString("Helen Leary"))`. The identical assertion already appears at line 117 inside `shouldListEverySpecialtyWithTheVeterinariansHoldingIt`. Both tests would fail on exactly the same defect — a missing full-name render — so the second test adds no independent behavioral signal and is pure duplication. The intent (first name precedes last name) is not separately verified; both tests only check that the concatenated string appears somewhere in the page.
findings.fix: Delete `shouldShowVeterinariansByFullName`. If first-before-last ordering must be independently tested, replace it with an assertion that checks the rendered order — e.g. verify the HTML position of the first-name token relative to the last-name token, or that 'Helen Leary' appears and 'Leary Helen' does not.

findings.description: PRD § Specialty directory edge case 2 is an explicit acceptance criterion: 'Specialties, and the veterinarians within each specialty, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one, and the no-specialty grouping holds a stable position among them.' No test exercises this. The controller sorts specialties by name (via SpecialtyRepository ORDER BY s.name) and sorts vets within each group by lastName then firstName, but neither ordering guarantee has a test. A regression that removes the sort — returning specialties in JPA iteration order or omitting the byFullName comparator — would pass the entire test suite undetected.

Inline comment `// radiology is held by Helen; surgery is held by no veterinarian.` narrates the test data relationship that the factory methods already express. docs/testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure prohibits inline comments that restate what the code says. The `helen()` factory at line 73-80 explicitly shows Helen holds radiology; surgery's absence from both factories conveys that it is unheld. The comment is redundant noise.
